correctness.rationale: For independent uniform endpoints, the supporting unoriented line has uniform angle theta in [0,pi) and independent signed arcsine distance s; because the target disk lies within the unit circle, segment and line hit events coincide. The exact arcsin integral is therefore valid. Fixed-r Taylor symmetry yields 4 K(r) epsilon/pi^2+O_r(epsilon^3); comparing the boundary integrand to K(1-epsilon(lambda-u)) and integrating the log singularity gives the stated two-term formula uniformly for bounded lambda>=1. Under alpha=epsilon^(w/2), each of the two angular branches has limiting conditional density 1/4 in (w,u), and Scheffe gives total variation. Fresh quadratures at lambda 1 and 2, epsilon=.01,.001 have residuals ~0.12–0.23 times epsilon^2 log(1/epsilon), consistent with the stated remainder. No claim for lambda divergent or a protruding target.

value.rationale: Endpoint-uniform chords are non-motion-invariant, and grazing a small disk near the sampling boundary has a nontrivial logarithmically enhanced rate. An explicit uniform boundary-layer crossover plus independent angular and displacement marks gives a meaningful rare-event geometric probability classification, not a mere restatement of a central chord distribution.
